pride_data.title: 2) Twisting Urea- to Imide-Based Mass Spectrometry-Cleavable Cross-Linkers to Embed Affinity Tags
pride_data.projectDescription: Disuccinimidyl dibutyric urea (DSBU) is a mass spectrometry (MS)-cleavable cross-linker that has been applied to multiple applications in structural biology, ranging from isolated protein complexes to comprehensive system-wide interactomics. DSBU facilitates a rapid and reliable identification of cross-links through the dissociation of its urea group in the gas-phase. In this study, we further advance the structural capabilities of DSBU by twisting the urea group into an imide, thus introducing a novel class of cross-linkers. This modification preserves the MS-cleavability of the amide bond, granted by the two acyl groups of the imide function. The central nitrogen atom enables the introduction of affinity purification tags. Here, we introduce disuccinimidyl dibutyric imide (DSBI) as prototype of this class of cross-linkers. It features a phosphonate handle for immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography (IMAC) enrichment. We detail DSBI synthesis and describe its behavior in solution and in the gas-phase while cross-linking isolated proteins and human cell lysates. DSBI and DSBU cross-links are compared at the same enrichment depths to bridge these two cross-linker classes. We validate DSBI cross-links by mapping them in high-resolution structures of large protein assemblies  . The cross-links observed yield insights into the morphology of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and their complexes. The DSBI linker might spearhead a novel class of MS-cleavable and enrichable cross-linkers

A solution containing 10 Î¼M Î±-synuclein in 50 mM HEPES, pH 7.4 was incubated at room temperature for 1 h with 1 mM DSBI. After washing with Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS) three times, cell pellets were resuspended in the cross-linking buffer (20 mM HEPES, 10 mM MgCl2, 150 mM KCl, 1%v/v DDM, pH 7.4). Cell debris were removed by centrifugation at 13,000 g for 15 min at 4Â°C. The supernatant was collected and adjusted to a final concentration of 1 mg/mL before carrying out the cross-linking reaction. 2 mM DSBI or DSBU was added and the reaction mixture was incubated for 1h at room temperature. The cross-linker was dissolved in neat DMSO immediately before adding it to the cell lysate. The reaction was quenched by adding ABC to a final concentration of 20 mM. Digestion of cross-linked samples. Cross-linked Î±-synuclein samples were denatured using urea (6M final concentration), diluted to 1 M urea before addition of trypsin (15:1 protein to enzyme ratio), incubated for 30 min followed by a second identical addition of the same protease, for a total digestion time of 2 hours. The proteolysis was quenched with trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) to a pH ~2. DSBI-Cross-linked HEK293T lysates (250 Âµg input) were snap-frozen and lyophilized. Samples were resuspended in 8M urea, reduced with 200 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) and alkylated with 100 mM iodoacetamide (IAA). Digestion was performed by adding trypsin (25:1 protein to enzyme ratio) for 30 min followed by a second identical addition of the same protease, for a total digestion time of 2 hours. The digestion was quenched with TFA to a pH ~2. DSBU-cross-linked HEK293T lysates (250 Âµg input) were proteolyzed in-solution with trypsin (25:1 protein to enzyme ratio) for 16 hours. Size Exclusion Chromatography of cross-linked HEK293T lysates. All three replicates of proteolyzed HEK293T lysates were subjected to size exclusion chromatography (SEC) on an Ã„KTA FPLC system (GE Healthcare), equipped with UPC-900, P-920 pump, and Frac-950 fraction collector (Amersham Biosciences) for pre-fractionation before LC-MS/MS analysis. Peptides were separated on a Superdex peptide 3.2/300 column (separation range 100-7000 Da, GE Healthcare) using a 2% (v/v) ACN, 0.1% (v/v) TFA solution at flow rate of 50 Âµl/min. 2 min fractions were collected over the whole run; fractions A12 to B9 were selected for subsequent LC-MS/MS analyses.  Mass Spectrometry Nano-ESI-LC-MS/MS analysis. Proteolyzed Î±-synuclein and HEK293T samples were analyzed via LC-MS/MS on an UltiMate 3000 RSLC nano-HPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) that was coupled to a timsTOF Pro mass spectrometer equipped with CaptiveSpray source (Bruker Daltonics). Peptides were trapped on a C18 column (precolumn Acclaim PepMap 100, 300 Î¼m Ã— 5 mm, 5 Î¼m, 100 Ã…, Thermo Fisher Scientific) at 50Â°C and separated on a self-packed Picofrit (New Objective) nanospray emitter (360 Î¼m o.d. Ã— 75 Î¼m i.d. x 400 mm L, 15 Î¼m Tip i.d.) with C18-stationary phase (3.0 Î¼m, 120 Ã…, Dr. Maisch GmbH). After trapping, peptides were eluted (column temerature 40Â°C) by a linear 90 min waterâˆ’acetonitrile (ACN) gradient from 3% (v/v) to 50% (v/v) ACN (Î±-synuclein samples) or by a linear 180 min gradient (HEK293T samples). Three biological replicates were analyzed for Î±-synuclein samples and HEK293T samples. Each biological replicate of the HEK293T sample was analyzed in technical duplicate. For the timsTOF Pro MS settings, the following parameters were adopted. The values for mobility-dependent collision energy ramping were set to 95 eV at an inverse reduced mobility (1/k0) of 1.6 V s/cm2 and 23 eV at 0.73 V s/cm2. Collision energies were linearly interpolated between these two 1/k0 values and kept constant above or below. No merging of TIMS scans was performed. Target intensity per individual PASEF precursor was set to 20000. The scan range was defined between 0.6 and 1.6 V s/cm2 with a ramp time/accumulation time of 166 ms. 14 PASEF MS/MS scans were triggered per cycle (2.57 s) with a maximum of seven precursors per mobilogram. Precursor ions in an m/z range between 100 and 1700 with charge states â‰¥ 3+ and â‰¤ 8+ were selected for fragmentation. pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: Identification of cross-links was performed with MeroX 2.0.1.7 (https://stavrox.com). The following settings were applied: proteolytic cleavage C-terminally at Lys and Arg, up to 5 missed cleavages (Î±-synuclein) or 3 missed cleavages (HEK293T samples) were allowed; peptide length: 5 to 30 amino acids; modifications: alkylation of Cys by iodoacetamide (fixed, only for HEK293T lysates), oxidation of Met (variable); cross-linker specificity: Lys, Ser, Thr, Tyr, N-terminus (Î±-synuclein) or Lys, Ser, N-terminus (HEK293T lysates); search algorithm: RISEUP mode (Î±-synuclein) with 3 maximum missing ions or Proteome-Wide mode (HEK293T samples) with a minimum peptide score of 10; precursor mass accuracy: 15 ppm; fragment ion mass accuracy: 25 ppm; signal-to-noise ratio > 1.5; precursor mass correction enabled (Î±-synuclein) and disabled (HEK293T lysates); false discovery rate (FDR) cut-off: 1%, and minimum score cut-off: 20. For Î±-synuclein samples, the fasta sequence of the protein was used for the MeroX search. For HEK293T lysates samples, 1 Âµg of DSBI and DSBU cross-linked samples were injected independently into the timsTOF and acquired with a 2+ to 8+ DDA-PASEF method. The identified proteins were used to build a cross-linker specific fasta database for carrying out the MeroX searches for all the proteome-wide XL-MS experiments which were performed.
